mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent housing recovery, which historically precedes a muted but positive equity market response over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically distinguishable from zero in at least 80% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that pressures firms to raise wages and prices, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days as profit growth expectations deteriorate.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below the previous year's minimum over four consecutive months signals a deepening consumption slump, which reliably precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < min(RSAFS last 12 months) for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.8%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 jobs alongside a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals an overheating labor market that precedes a positive S&P 500 return over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate earnings upgrades.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive trend in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over a six-month rolling window signals improving manufacturing activity that supports earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of all periods where the INDPRO trend condition is met.
